facts.statement: The genus was first described in 1932 by Danish paleontologist Eigil Nielsen.
facts.quote: The first fossils of Fadenia were discovered and described in the periodical Meddelelser om Grønland in 1932 by the Danish vertebrate palaeontologist Eigil Nielsen

facts.statement: Nielsen discovered the fossils while participating in the Three-year Expedition to East Greenland led by Lauge Koch.
facts.quote: Nielsen had joined at the beginning of the Three-year Expedition to East Greenland led by Danish geologist and explorer Lauge Koch.

facts.statement: The genus name Fadenia honors Gunnar Seidenfaden, the manager of the expedition.
facts.quote: The manager of the expedition was the botanist Gunnar Seidenfaden, after whose surname the genus was named.

facts.statement: Fadenia fossils have been found in the Carboniferous of Missouri, the Permian of Greenland, and the Early Triassic of British Columbia.
facts.quote: Fadenia is an extinct genus of eugeneodontid holocephalian chondrichthyan from the Carboniferous Period of Missouri (United States), the Permian period of Greenland, and the Early Triassic epoch of British Columbia, Canada (Sulphur Mountain Formation).

facts.statement: Fadenia is a member of the order Eugeneodontida, which is defined by the presence of tooth whorls.
facts.quote: Fadenia belongs to Eugeneodontida, an extinct order of Chondrichthyes that are characterized by the presence of tooth whorls.

facts.statement: Individuals of this genus could grow to approximately 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: It could reach about 1.5 m in length.

facts.statement: Fadenia was one of the few eugeneodont genera to survive the end-Permian mass extinction and represents one of the latest survivors of the group.
facts.quote: Fadenia is one of the few eugeneodont genera that survived the end-Permian mass extinction event, and it was one of the latest-surviving members of this clade.

facts.statement: A later classification authority for the genus is P. Aellen and C. C. Townsend, 1972.
facts.quote: genus_authority: P. Aellen & C. C. Townsend, 1972

facts.statement: Fadenia is classified within the family Caseodontidae.
Fadenia is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Eugeneodontiformes.
facts.quote: Fadenia es un género extinto de peces cartilaginosos del orden Eugeneodontiformes

facts.statement: Two species are recognized within the genus: Fadenia crenulata and Fadenia gigas.
facts.quote: Se reconocen dos especies de Fadenia: Fadenia crenulata Fadenia gigas
